readout_other: blood pressure, heart rate, respiration rate, heart rate variability, systolic BP variability, baroreflex sensitivity; H&E staining of vagus nerve
direction_notes: Left vagus nerve FUS lowered blood pressure and respiration rate, reduced normalised low-frequency HRV power and LF/HF ratio (sympathetic inhibition) and raised normalised high-frequency HRV power (parasympathetic activation) versus controls; effects persisted about 30 min after FUS.
safety_notes: H&E histology of the sonicated vagus nerve showed normal histology without necrosis or inflammatory response.

exposures.label: FUS of the left cervical vagus nerve

timing.protocol_description: 100 Hz PRF, 20% duty cycle, 2 ms tone burst, 1 s sonication, inter-stimulation interval of 6 s; each trial had 10 min baseline, 15 min ultrasound stimulation and 30 min recovery. Control-sham: transducer placed on the nerve with FUS off; Control-FUS: FUS to the left upper leg.

source_quotes.n_subjects: In order to evaluate the effects on autonomic function by FUS of the vagus nerve, Fifty 12-week-old spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs, all male, body weight 284  54 g) were randomly divided into three groups: Control-sham (n = 21), Control-FUS (n = 12), and FUS (n = 17) group.

flags.reason: 50 rats were allocated to three groups; 21 (Control-sham) received no ultrasound, 12 received FUS at the leg and 17 at the vagus nerve. Value is enrolled total.
Stated Ispta 0.6 W/cm2 is not what 20% duty cycle times 18 W/cm2 would give; the 1 s on / 6 s interval pattern may explain it. Recorded as stated.
Paper states the control groups were meant to exclude auditory and non-target confounds; no dedicated auditory control (masking, deafening) is described.
Transducer maker not named; described only by frequency, diameter and focal length; refers to a previous paper.
Trials are counted per group (25, 25, 15 trials) and not per rat.
